# Review pack: Ayyub

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/ayyub.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the narrative, not a chronology the Quran claims; verses come from several surahs and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about Ayyub. None is used in this draft.
- The Quran does not say what the harm of Ayyub was. The draft uses its words, harm, hardship and suffering, and gives no description of an illness or of a loss.
- 38:44 (the bundle and the word tahnath) and 38:42 (strike with the foot) are stated in their own words only and a scholar should look at them first.
- The phrase his family and the like of them with them (21:84, 38:43) is left open between the same people returned and others given.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Ayyub's wife and the details of his illness and of his lost goods and children. None is used in the story texts.
- Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Ayyub calls to his Lord  (`#the-call-in-hardship`)

Cited ayat: 21:83, 38:41

> **21:83** وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

> **38:41** وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ

### Claims

**c1** (21:83): Ayyub called to his Lord that harm had touched him, and that He is the most merciful of those who show mercy.

**c2** (38:41): The Quran tells its hearer to mention Ayyub, whom God calls His servant, when he called to his Lord that Satan had touched him with hardship and suffering.

### One-minute summary

Ayyub called to his Lord that harm had touched him [c1]. He said that Satan had touched him with hardship and suffering [c2].

### Complete story

Ayyub called to his Lord that harm had touched him, and that He is the most merciful of those who show mercy [c1].

In another passage the Quran tells its hearer to mention Ayyub, whom God calls His servant, when he called to his Lord that Satan had touched him with hardship and suffering [c2].

### Deep study

The calls are told in different words and are placed together here by theme [c1][c2]. The first names the harm and then the mercy of God [c1]. The later one speaks of Satan touching him with hardship and suffering [c2]. The Quran does not say what the harm was [c1][c2].

### Kids mode

Ayyub called to his Lord that harm had touched him [c1]. He said that his Lord is the most merciful of those who show mercy [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ayyub calls on his Lord by naming his harm and then naming God's mercy [c1]. Another is that the Quran has God call him His servant at the moment it tells of his call [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the harm, the hardship and the suffering were, how long they lasted, or when and where Ayyub lived.
- Not established: how Satan touched him with hardship and suffering (38:41); the verse gives his words and nothing more.
- Not established: whether the calls were made at the same time.

## 2. The answer to Ayyub  (`#the-answer-and-the-restoration`)

Cited ayat: 21:84, 38:42-44

> **21:84** فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ

> **38:42** ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هَٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌۢ بَارِدٌ وَشَرَابٌ
>
> **38:43** وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
>
> **38:44** وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًا فَٱضْرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحْنَثْ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَٰهُ صَابِرًا نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌ

### Claims

**c1** (21:84): God responded to Ayyub and removed the harm that was on him.

**c2** (21:84): God gave Ayyub his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Him and a reminder for those who worship.

**c3** (38:42): God told Ayyub to strike with his foot, and said that this was a cool place of washing and a drink.

**c4** (38:43): God granted Ayyub his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Him and a reminder for those with understanding.

**c5** (38:44): God told Ayyub to take a bundle in his hand and strike with it, and not to fall into tahnath, an Arabic word for failing in something one is bound by.

**c6** (38:44): God found Ayyub patient, said that he was an excellent servant, and said that he turned back to God often.

### One-minute summary

God responded to Ayyub and removed the harm that was on him [c1]. He gave Ayyub his family and the like of them with them [c2][c4]. God found him patient, an excellent servant who turned back to Him often [c6].

### Complete story

God responded to Ayyub and removed the harm that was on him [c1]. God gave Ayyub his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Him and a reminder for those who worship [c2].

In another passage God told Ayyub to strike with his foot, and said that this was a cool place of washing and a drink [c3]. God granted Ayyub his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Him and a reminder for those with understanding [c4]. God told Ayyub to take a bundle in his hand and strike with it, and not to fall into tahnath, an Arabic word for failing in something one is bound by [c5]. God found Ayyub patient, said that he was an excellent servant, and said that he turned back to God often [c6].

### Deep study

The answer is told at 21:84 in parts, the removal of the harm and the gift of the family [c1][c2]. The passage at 38:42-44 adds a command to strike with the foot, with a cool place of washing and a drink [c3]; the gift of the family again [c4]; and a command about a bundle, followed by God's words of praise for Ayyub [c5][c6]. The gifts of the family are told in nearly the same words [c2][c4].

### Kids mode

God responded to Ayyub and removed the harm that was on him [c1]. God gave him his family and the like of them with them [c2][c4]. God found Ayyub patient, an excellent servant [c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran presents the gift to Ayyub as a mercy from God and a reminder for those who worship [c2][c4]. Another is that the passage ends with God's praise of Ayyub as patient and as one who turned back to Him often [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what Ayyub struck with his foot, or how the cool place of washing and the drink came about; the verse 38:42 does not name an object.
- Not established: what the family were, whether the same people were returned to him or others were given, or how the like of them is to be counted.
- Not established: what the bundle was, what it was struck on, or what Ayyub was bound by; the verse says only that he was not to fall into tahnath. A reviewer should look at this wording first.
- Not established: how long the harm lasted before it was removed, or his age.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the name of Ayyub's wife and the details of his illness. None is used in the story texts.
